# Overview

Here is my initial exploration of participant demographics.

Here are my research questions:\
- How many respondents took the survey, and from how many institutions?\
- Which regions are those institutions located in?\
- What roles do our respondents represent?\
- What are our respondents' professional backgrounds?\


# Import packages, utilities, and config variables
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(docstring)
library(readr)

source("utils.R")

# Read config.yml
cfg <- config::get()
```


# Load data

```{r}
mc_complex <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "mc_complex.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
mc_other <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "mc_other.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
prof_bg <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "prof_bg.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
sata_other <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "sata_other.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
qual <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "qual.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
qual_pii <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "qual_pii.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# How many respondents took the survey?

```{r}
nrow(mc_complex)

```

The numbers above^ should match, and this represents the number of respondents.

# How many institutions?

I'm commenting out the relevant code for privacy reasons, but I first manually inspected the responses.
```{r}
# Keep commented for privacy!!
# qual_pii$institution
```

Looking at the responses, I see several "categories" of institution: Network, networked university campus, independent university campus, and university-affiliated research center. "Networked" refers specifically to an OSPO network, not any other kind of network. Grouping the institutions by category, rather than listing them, will help protect respondent anonymity.

I have manually cleaned up the responses (a lot of people listed their OSPO/department as well as their institution) and listed the responses, categories, and regions in data/manually_curated/orgs.tsv.

```{r}
# Do not preview in notebook, for privacy!!
orgs <- read_tsv(
  file.path(cfg$curated_path, "orgs.tsv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_names = c("org", "cat", "region")
)

orgs <- orgs |>
  count(across(all_of(c("org", "cat", "region"))), name = "cnt")

# This is the number of unique institutions
nrow(orgs)

orgs <- orgs |>
  arrange(desc(cnt))

# Write to file (from utils.R)
write_df_to_file(orgs, "orgs_summary.tsv", path_key = "curated_path")

# Summary of org categories
table(orgs$cat)
```

# Which regions are those institutions located in?

```{r}

```

^The table above shows represented regions.

# What are our respondents' professional backgrounds?

```{r}
# Returns a list containing the frequency table for each column
table_list <- lapply(prof_bg, table)

# Examined the output by eye to make sure there's no weirdness
# table_list

# Extract the "Yes" count for each professional background
# This was a SATA question so total != # of respondents
yes_counts <- sapply(table_list, function(x) x["Yes"])
yes_counts <- sort(yes_counts, decreasing = TRUE)
print(yes_counts)
```

Examining the "other" responses. Mostly it looks like people just elaborating on the responses above, though one person said they were previously a volunteer to OS projects, which is interesting.
